As predicted, 7/7/6 RL rounds fit instead of 5/5/4 and RL solved 1203 targets against 1149. The eval gap did not move: 672 at 2 loops, so 8 loops add +18 (23/19/13), the same as 500. This improves RL; it does not make loops pay more at eval. The surprise is the randomized retries. I predicted depth would stop mattering on resistant targets after round 2; it did not. Of the targets that failed 8 tries at 1 loop, pooled over seeds and rounds (about 4,100 per arm, 24 tries each), 11.4% got a proof at 2 loops, 13.8% at 4 and 15.9% at 8 (per-sample acceptance 2.3%, 3.6%, 4.7%). In rounds 3+ it is still 10.4%, 11.7%, 14.3%, and 8 loops beat 2 in every seed (67 vs 57, 99 vs 58, 121 vs 95 targets), unlike the spike's flat curve on never-solved targets. Two caveats: the retry set is selected on failing at 1 loop, which favours loop counts least like 1 loop, and an 8-loop sample costs about 2x a 2-loop one, so per GPU-second 2 loops still cracks more. | 504-claude | Truncated backprop through the loops: only the last 2 passes get gradient, earlier passes hand over a no-grad draft state | claude-opus-5-5 | loops, loss, rl | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 24 | 662 | 670 | 1209 | discard | 0.9615 | 0.0898 | 306 403 506 613 863 887 930 978 1028 1051 1071 1086 1100 1108 1119 1133 1138 1143 1148 1159 1167 1171 1176 1185 1190 1194 1197 1200 1204 1205 1208 1209 1211 1216 1221 1223 | 3526 | 662 at 8 loops (seeds 662/674/651) against 690: -28, and below the 2-loop diagnostic on every seed (676/682/652, mean 670), so metric minus diag went from 502's +18 (23/19/13) to -8 (-14/-8/-1). The pre-registered falsifier fired: after RL, 8 loops no longer beat 2. Per-sample dev accuracy 0.433/0.404/0.402 at 8 loops against 0.427/0.417/0.403 at 2 (502: 0.466/0.489/0.460 against 0.435/0.461/0.436). The 2-loop theorem count is unchanged (670 against 672) though its per-sample accuracy is lower, so in theorems the whole loss is the depth benefit. The throughput half of the prediction held and bought nothing: 4,858/4,780/4,774 pretraining steps (1.40x, as benchmarked) left val loss at 2 loops at 0.0898/0.0830/0.0852 (mean 0.0860 against 0.0866; predicted at or below 0.085), and 9/9/8 RL rounds against 7/7/6 solved 1,209 targets against 1,203. At equal round count the fine-tuned model was behind: 1-loop accuracy on RL targets 0.696/0.681 after 6 fine-tunes on seeds 0/1 against 0.73/0.74, and 0.677 against 0.731 after 5 on seed 2. The retry comparison shows where depth went. On the pretrained model deeper retries still helped (round-1 per-sample acceptance at 2/4/8 loops 0.045/0.069/0.089, 0.049/0.078/0.077, 0.014/0.020/0.026 by seed) and pretraining val loss at 8 loops was at or below 2 loops on every seed, so truncation did not break deep passes in pretraining. After fine-tuning the advantage was gone: pooled over seeds and rounds, resistant targets were cracked 11.4% at 2 loops, 12.7% at 4 and 12.6% at 8 (502: 11.4/13.8/15.9), and in rounds 3+ 9.2/9.6/9.3 (502: 10.4/11.7/14.3). Interpretation, not established: the premise that passes before the last two carry no useful gradient is wrong. With truncation the first core pass, which does most of the work (1 loop reaches 0.72 on RL targets), is differentiated only at loop counts 1 and 2, a quarter of the batches, so each step teaches the shared core less; and the +18 that 8 loops buy in 500 and 502 looks like something full backprop through the unrolled passes builds on the long RL proofs. Next: if throughput is wanted, narrow the loop range with full backprop (the spike's 1-4 arm) instead of cutting the gradient; if depth is wanted, the lever is more end-to-end gradient through deep unrolls on hard proofs, not less. |
| 505-fable | Countdown embedding: every pass of the shared core is told how many passes remain before its state is decoded | claude-fable-5-1 | architecture, loops | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 56 | 681 | 662 | 1181 | discard | 0.958 | 0.0791 | 424 493 582 676 861 889 931 962 1011 1020 1044 1067 1087 1094 1109 1124 1131 1136 1147 1159 1163 1172 1177 1183 1185 1186 1187 1191 | 3451 | 681 at 8 loops (678/710/655) against 502's 690 (687/715/669): -9, inside noise, discard. This is the 'signal ignored' branch of the preregistration, with one nuance. The countdown rows were learned but stayed small: after RL their norms were 0.41-0.93 against an entry-output norm of 20 (2-5%; the pre-registered 'used' threshold was 25%, 'ignored' below 5%), largest for rows 3-6 (passes far from the end) and smallest for rows 0-1. The iteration still converges fast: the relative change of the core state per pass at 8 loops after RL was 0.28, 0.10, 0.046, 0.025, 0.017, 0.016 and then 0.022-0.027 on the last pass. That final uptick is the one visible use of the countdown, on every seed (0.012 to 0.020 after pretraining, 0.016 to 0.027 after RL): the countdown-0 pass does a small distinct 'finalize' step while passes 4-7 sit near a fixed point. The loop gap did not move: metric minus diag +19 (17/22/18; 502: +18, 500: +18). Per-sample dev accuracy at 8 vs 2 loops 0.470/0.489/0.435 vs 0.437/0.457/0.406, a gap of 0.033 against about 0.02 on 502 seed 0, but the 8-loop accuracy itself is not above 502's 0.48. The surprise is pretraining: val loss at 2 loops 0.079/0.082/0.076 (mean 0.079 against 502's 0.087), the lowest of this loop so far, with a small depth dependence appearing on two seeds (1 loop 0.0836 vs 0.0820 at 8 on seed 1, 0.0805 vs 0.0758 on seed 2, seed 0 flat within 0.0001), and none of it carried to RL or eval. The 1-loop program got slightly weaker, which 502's 1-loop-first schedule pays for: round-1 one-loop acceptance 0.137/0.024/0.044 (502: 0.159/0.038/0.052), cumulative RL solved 1181 (1191/1192/1160 vs 1203). RL rounds 7/6/6 (502: 7/7/6); seeds 1 and 2 each missed a 7th round by the 15% margin (232 s and 238 s left against about 245 s needed). Steps 3460/3408/3469, 6,403,328 params, no speed change, no crash. Interpretation: letting the core know how many passes remain is necessary but not sufficient for a non-converged iteration; with the same next-token loss at every depth, gradient descent keeps the converged one-pass-plus-refinement program and uses the budget signal only to adjust the final pass. Next: a loss that only deep passes can lower (depth-dependent targets, or a loop distribution without n = 1 combined with the countdown so intermediate states are never decoded), or spend the spare 3.6M parameters, since 502's model is at least as parameter-limited as depth-limited. |
| 506-claude | Untied first pass: pass 1 of the loop gets its own two blocks, the shared core only refines (9.56M parameters, same compute per loop count) | claude-opus-5-5 | architecture, loops | 0.5 | 5400/300/1800 | 23 | 665 | 654 | 1174 | discard | 0.9425 | 0.0811 | 147 206 268 317 706 766 820 874 919 953 989 1023 1047 1059 1073 1096 1113 1122 1133 1140 1148 1152 1160 1167 | 3309 | 665 at 8 loops (seeds 652/688/655) against 690 (687/715/669): -25, below 502 on every seed (-35/-27/-14). Both pre-registered effects failed. Capacity: six unique blocks at 2 loops scored 654 (635/675/653) against the tied trunk's 672, per-sample dev accuracy 0.388/0.408/0.408 against 0.435/0.461/0.435 (predicted at least 680 and 0.45), although pretraining did fit better as predicted (val loss at 2 loops 0.0811/0.0814/0.0857, mean 0.0827 against 0.0866; 3,355/3,378/3,377 steps). Refinement: metric minus diag was +11 (17/13/2) against 502's +18 (predicted at least +25; seed 2's +2 is no gain), and per-sample dev accuracy rose from 2 to 8 loops by 0.024/0.038/0.027, mean 0.030, against 502's 0.028 (predicted at least 0.04). A shared core that only ever refines buys the same +0.03 per sample from six more applications as a core that also does the first pass, so the dual role is not what limits depth. The retry arm of the falsifier fired: targets that failed 8 tries at 1 loop were cracked 21.9% of the time at 2 loops, 23.6% at 4 and 23.9% at 8, pooled (1.09x from 2 to 8; 502: 11.4/13.8/15.9, 1.39x), and on seed 0 8 loops cracked fewer than 2 (250 against 276 of 1,394). The gap arm stopped just short (+10.7 against a threshold of +10). The loop is not vestigial, but the step that matters is now 1 loop to 2, the shared core's first application: the 2-loop crack rate is nearly double 502's because the 1-loop model is much weaker, and that is where the run was lost. After 5 fine-tunes, 1-loop per-sample accuracy on RL targets was 0.583/0.588/0.592 against 502's 0.715/0.718/0.731 at the same round (predicted 0.69-0.75), though pretraining left the 1-loop path as good as 502's (val loss at 1 loop 0.0840/0.0819/0.0921 against 0.0859/0.0825/0.0950; 1 loop minus 2 loops +0.0029/+0.0005/+0.0064, mean +0.0032, the bottom of the predicted range). More targets failed the cheap pass (402/382/397 in round 6 against 343/335/333), rounds after the first averaged 263 s against 241 s, and seeds 0 and 1 lost their 7th round with 176 s and 100 s left (6/6/6 rounds, predicted 7/7/6). The retries made up for the weak first pass in discovery: cumulative RL solved after 6 rounds was 1,167/1,188/1,166 against 502's 1,171/1,191/1,196 at round 6 (final 1,174 against 1,203). The lost round does not explain the result: on seed 2, where both runs had 6 rounds, this is still -14 at 8 loops, and per-sample dev accuracy at 8 loops is lower on every seed (0.412/0.446/0.435 against 0.466/0.489/0.460). Interpretation, not established: in the tied trunk every batch at any depth trains the weights that the 1-loop pass runs and is decoded from, which is why 1 loop stays within about 0.05 of 8 loops on RL targets there (500); untied, the first-pass blocks are decoded directly in 1 fine-tune batch in 8 and otherwise learn to feed the core, and each untied block gets one application's gradient per step of a 600-step fine-tune. Weight tying is doing useful work for RL, and 3.16M more parameters with a better pretraining loss gave a fine-tuned model that is worse on dev at both depths, so parameters are not the bottleneck under this budget. Next: keep the first pass tied. The gain from 2 to 8 loops has been +0.02 to +0.03 per sample in 500, 502 and here, whatever the core was asked to do, which points away from the core's role and toward what the training data demands of depth. |
| 507-fable | RL fine-tune in token-budget batches: the same 76,800 records per round in ~3x fewer padded tokens, so more RL rounds fit | claude-fable-5-1 | rl, systems | 0.5 | 5400/300/1800 | 55 | 732 | 714 | 1246 | keep | 0.9435 | 0.0815 | 372 441 506 591 797 831 890 953 1029 1045 1064 1090 1109 1122 1144 1155 1161 1163 1171 1175 1180 1186 1194 1199 1202 1205 1211 1217 1220 1225 1235 1239 1242 1242 1246 1250 1255 1255 1256 1257 1258 1258 1261 1265 | 3775 | 732 at 8 loops (seeds 746/765/684) against 502's 690 (687/715/669): +42, the first result in this loop above the spike's 700 bar; keep. The mechanism went as predicted and then some. The fine-tune (level-1 call interval minus its sampling time, which also holds the Lean judge) fell to 51-73 s per round over 579-770 token-budget steps, against about 150 s for the same quantity in 505 (502's RL code on a normal pod), so the fine-tune itself is about 2.5x faster; a round charged to the RL clock fell from about 245 s (502) to 170-195 s on seeds 0/1 and 200-230 s on seed 2, whose weak start sent more targets to retries. 11/11/9 RL rounds fit (502: 7/7/6; predicted 9-10) and RL solved 1265/1264/1208, mean 1246 (502: 1203; predicted 1210-1260). Pretraining is byte-identical: 3338/3443/3461 steps, val at 2 loops 0.0815/0.0868/0.0780. Loops, unchanged by design: metric minus diag +18 (20/22/10; 502: +18, 500: +18); diag 714 (726/743/674; 502: 672), so the whole gain is at both depths and the 8-vs-2 gap did not move. The surprise is where the gain sits. Per-sample dev accuracy barely moved, 0.480/0.483/0.445 at 8 loops (502: 0.466/0.489/0.460) and 0.445/0.445/0.417 at 2 (502: 0.435/0.461/0.436), yet pass@64 rose by 50-60 theorems on seeds 0/1 at every length (seed 0 vs 502 seed 0, lengths 7-13: 112/121/379/100/25/7/2 vs 105/111/360/84/21/5/1), and last-round 1-loop RL acceptance was slightly lower, 0.716/0.703/0.678 (502: 0.730/0.740/0.731; one seed under my 0.70 line, the falsifier needed two). So the extra rounds bought sample diversity, not per-sample accuracy: the 64 attempts cover more theorems at the same hit rate. Candidate causes, not established: more rounds means the found-proof sets are larger and reshuffled into the mix more times (up to 4 distinct proofs per target), and length-homogeneous batches may weight long proofs differently from mixed batches; separating rounds from batching needs a run with the new batching capped at 7 rounds. Round-1 yield predicted nothing again: seed 1 started at 34 targets (1-loop acceptance 0.007) and finished highest at 765. Deeper retries still crack more resistant targets: pooled over seeds and rounds 11.0% at 2 loops, 13.5% at 4, 14.1% at 8 (502: 11.4/13.8/15.9), rounds 3+ 11.5/13.1/13.3. Caveat on the baseline: 502 seed 0's pod sampled at 1 loop at 107-128 samples/s in rounds 2-4 against 220-270 here and 205-237 on 500/503/504/505, so part of 502's 245 s rounds was its pod; the fine-tune comparison above uses 505. 55 patch lines, all in finetune() and token_batches(first=); no crash, pods 68-73 min. Next: a round is now about a third fine-tune, the rest 1-loop sampling and Lean judging, so cheap rounds can be spent deeper (more 8-loop retries, or a second deep pass on targets still resisting after round 6), or the Muon fine-tune the program lists, since the fine-tune now runs 7,000-8,000 steps per run, twice pretraining's. |
| 508-claude | Train on 1-4 loops instead of 1-8: the scored 8-loop eval reads out a fixed point no batch pays to train | claude-opus-5-5 | loops, schedule | 0.5 | 5400/300/1800 | 6 | 683 | 678 | 1221 | discard | 0.9665 | 0.0808 | 445 497 555 606 754 787 826 861 941 959 982 1004 1039 1047 1060 1075 1094 1098 1108 1117 1133 1138 1140 1144 1156 1159 1161 1165 1170 1173 1177 1182 1184 1186 1189 1194 1197 1197 1198 1200 | 3439 | 683 at 8 loops (seeds 676/699/673) against 690 (687/715/669): -7 (-11/-16/+4), inside noise, discard by the rule. metric and metric_diag are within noise of each other (683 against 678 at 2 loops: 664/710/661), so this model is no better at 8 loops than at 2. The speed half of the prediction held in full. Pretraining took 4,777/4,896/4,700 steps (1.40x 502; predicted 4,900-5,400, just under) and val loss at 2 loops was 0.0808/0.0784/0.0848 (mean 0.0813 against 0.0866). The fine-tune cost 74-104 s a round against 120-163 s, so 10/9/9 RL rounds fit against 7/7/6, RL solved 1,221 targets (1200/1253/1211) against 1,203, and last-round 1-loop accuracy on RL targets was 0.781/0.806/0.781 against 0.730/0.740/0.731 (0.750/0.778/0.763 already at round 7). The untrained depth did not break: val loss at 8 loops was within 0.0002 of 4 loops on every seed, and on the pretrained model the round-1 retries cracked resistant targets 15.8% of the time at 2 loops, 19.0% at 4 and 19.9% at 8 (502, trained on 1-8: 14.6/19.3/20.7), so a model that never trained past 4 loops gets the same lift from 8 as one that did. Pooled over all rounds 8 loops stayed within 0.4 points of 4 as predicted (9.4/10.9/11.3% at 2/4/8), and per-sample dev accuracy at 8 loops rose to 0.484/0.487/0.480 from 0.466/0.489/0.460. What went the other way is the gap this loop exists to grow. metric minus diag fell to +4 (12/-11/12) from +18 (23/19/13); on seed 1, 8 loops solved 11 fewer theorems than 2 loops (the pre-registered readout falsifier needed two such seeds, so it did not fire). Per-sample dev accuracy at 2 loops rose by 0.031 (0.470/0.486/0.470 against 0.435/0.461/0.436) and at 8 loops by 0.011, so 8 loops now add +0.008 per sample (0.014/0.001/0.010) where 502 had +0.028. In RL the edge of 8 loops over 4 on resistant targets that 502 showed (15.9% against 13.8% pooled, 14.9 against 12.2 in rounds 3-6) is gone (11.3 against 10.9; 8.2 against 8.1). All retry rates were below my predicted 11-16%: at matched rounds 3-6 resistant targets were cracked 6.4/8.1/8.2% of the time at 2/4/8 loops against 502's 11.1/12.2/14.9%, with failed sets of about the same size on seed 0 (560/461/407/367 against 540/450/390/343). The surprise is that higher per-sample accuracy at both depths bought no theorems. The model got sharper, not broader: at 8 loops, dev theorems solved on 48 or more of the 64 attempts rose to 497 (501/496/494) from 483 (469/503/476), theorems solved on only 1-15 attempts fell to 89 (85/95/86) from 103 (106/111/93), and unsolved went from 418 to 425. The 2-3 extra RL rounds added 44/42/33 targets after round 7's first pass. Interpretation, not established: the metric counts the tail of rarely-solved theorems, which is fed by the spread of the sampling distribution; more fine-tune rounds and better-trained shallow passes concentrate probability on proofs the model already finds, which raises per-sample accuracy and lowers the crack rate on what is left. That is the third time more rounds or lower val loss failed to reach the metric (504: 9/9/8 rounds; 505: val 0.079). On depth: the 8-loop state of a 1-4 model is a usable fixed point, as the spike said, but the small advantage of 8 loops over 2 after RL (most of 502's +18) depends on training at 5-8 loops, or on 2 loops being under-trained in the 1-8 model, which this run cannot separate; either way the 1-8 range is not pure cost for this metric. No crash; totals 3,335/3,439/3,435 s. Next: the cheaper 1-4 model is equal within noise, so the saved time is better spent on spread than on rounds (more attempts or a higher oracle temperature on the retries, fewer fine-tune steps per round); and a 1-4 range with an occasional 8-loop batch would separate the two readings of the lost gap. |

Yet cumulative RL solved is 1,265/1,260/1,246 (507: 1,265/1,264/1,208), identical on seeds 0 and 1: the better-fitting model found the same targets, and pass@64 at 8 loops moved at lengths 7-8 (seed 0: 123/124 against 112/121) and not at 9+ (380/94/26/6 against 379/100/25/7), seed 1 mixed (-16 at length 8, +6 at 9). The converse of 507: that run raised coverage with flat per-sample accuracy; this one raises per-sample accuracy with flat coverage, because the proofs it samples more reliably are ones 64 attempts already found. Loops, unchanged by design and in fact: metric minus diag +21 (25/24/13; 507: +18 = 20/22/10), per-sample 8-vs-2 gap 0.027/0.028/0.031 (507: 0.035/0.038/0.028), retries pooled 11.8/14.7/15.8% cracked at 2/4/8 loops (507: 11.0/13.5/14.1), rounds 3+ 10.1/11.9/12.7 (507: 11.5/13.1/13.3), per-sample retry acceptance 0.036/0.053/0.062 (507: 0.033/0.051/0.057); the speculative Muon-on-refinement-directions effect (gap above +28 on two seeds) did not appear. Cost as benched: fine-tune time per round 54-73 s, mean 66/66/67 s (507: 65/64/59), so the graphed Muon step adds 1-2 s a round; ft_steps 588-762; RL charged 1,650/1,690/1,747 s with 150/110/53 s left; no forgetting signal (held-out greedy after RL 0.985/0.986/0.985). Pretraining is the same code (MuonStep is pretraining's capture code moved; bench 13.1-13.9 steps/s as the incumbent): 3,429/3,428/3,351 steps, val at 2 loops 0.0872/0.0877/0.0834 against 507's 0.0815/0.0868/0.0780, worse by 0.006/0.001/0.005, inside the spread the unchanged code shows across runs (503: 0.089/0.085/0.084), and depth-flat within 0.0003 from 2 to 8 loops as always. Interpretation, not established: with up to 4 proofs per target weighted x4 and two passes over 76,800 records, the fine-tune already fits the found proofs about as well as the data allows, so a better optimizer sharpens the policy on them (per-sample accuracy up, the 1-loop pass stronger) without widening what 64 eval attempts reach; 3e-3 was not too hot, and a higher Muon lr or momentum kept across rounds is untested. 85 patch lines (+54/-31), about 35 of them the helper extraction. Next: the RL bottleneck is now what the fine-tune is fed, not how it is fit. A run that spends the leftover 50-150 s per seed and the cheaper rounds on more attempts for the 235-254 targets never solved, or that raises the 1-loop sampling temperature to buy diversity, tests that directly; the loop gap has not moved in nine experiments and still needs a loss that only deep passes can lower. |
| 510-fable | More, shorter RL rounds: half the fine-tune records per round (38,400 instead of 76,800), so about 16 rounds of expert iteration fit in RL_SECS instead of 11 | claude-fable-5-1 | rl, schedule | 0.5 | 5400/300/1800 | 11 | 764 | 752 | 1274 | keep | 0.9425 | 0.0824 | 139 167 220 261 589 640 738 846 966 990 1028 1065 1086 1099 1119 1140 1153 1158 1167 1174 1180 1186 1192 1199 1203 1206 1209 1211 1212 1213 1217 1219 1220 1222 1226 1231 1234 1234 1238 1239 1240 1244 1246 1250 1254 1258 1260 1261 1261 1263 1264 1264 | 3941 | 764 at 8 loops (743/815/734) against 509's 748 (755/761/728): +16, keep by the rule, not shown beyond noise: seeds 0 and 2 moved -12 and +6 and the mean gain is seed 1 (+54, 815, the highest single seed in this loop). The hypothesis was half right and the half that worked was the one I called secondary. Rounds rose less than computed: 13/14/12 (509: 11/11/11; predicted 14-17), so the pre-registered 'rounds did not rise' falsifier fired on two seeds. The fine-tune did halve (ft_steps 294-399 against 588-762), but late rounds only fell from 129-157 s to 102-133 s because the retry calls grew: the weaker one-loop pass sent more targets to 2/4/8-loop retries (2,091/1,836/1,992 retry-target slots against 1,754/1,580/1,671) and each pass returned more proofs to judge (Lean samples 452k/446k/433k against 404k/391k/398k). Fit got clearly worse, as the 'fine-tune volume matters' branch predicted: last-round 1-loop acceptance on RL targets 0.671/0.667/0.634 (509: 0.734/0.731/0.736; all three under my 0.70 line), 0.665/0.668/0.663 at matched round 11 (-0.07, predicted -0.02 to -0.05), round-2 acceptance 0.231/0.410/0.292 (509: 0.368/0.441/0.426), and per-sample dev accuracy fell by about 0.03 at both depths: 0.461/0.481/0.443 at 8 loops (509: 0.492/0.492/0.471) and 0.422/0.444/0.417 at 2 (509: 0.465/0.464/0.440). Yet that branch's metric prediction (below 735) did not follow: the model samples each proof less reliably and covers more theorems, 507's pattern again. The policy is visibly less peaked: new distinct proofs per late one-loop pass 546-608 (seed 0), 809-1,089 (seed 1), 757-847 (seed 2) against 509's 481-567, 419-438, 390-443, i.e. 1.3-2.5x more at similar solved counts, and distinct proofs handed back by the last pass 3,347/4,165/3,405 (509: 3,076/3,014/2,877). Cumulative RL solved 1,264/1,314/1,243 (509: 1,265/1,260/1,246): identical on seeds 0 and 2, +54 on seed 1, and the eval tracked it seed by seed. So two things moved together and this run cannot separate them: 2-3 more sampling passes, and 1.2-1.9 epochs per round instead of 2.4-3.7 leaving a higher-entropy policy; the per-seed pairing of RL solved with dev solved suggests the discovery side. Loops: metric minus diag shrank to +12 (12/20/5) from +21 (25/24/13), and on seed 2 metric and metric_diag (734 against 729) are within noise of each other, so this model is no better at 8 loops than at 2 there; per sample the 8-vs-2 gap is unchanged (0.039/0.037/0.026 against 0.027/0.028/0.031), the theorem gap is what narrowed. Retry crack rates pooled 15.1/18.1/19.0, 20.0/23.8/24.9, 15.3/17.0/17.1% at 2/4/8 loops (509: 11.4/14.6/15.3, 12.3/15.8/17.3, 11.7/13.7/14.9), higher because the failed sets are larger and easier (selection), and in rounds 3+ depth no longer orders them on seeds 0 and 2 (17.7/16.8/18.2 and 17.3/17.5/17.0; 509: 10.7/11.4/12.8 and 9.3/11.2/11.2). Pretraining identical up to nondeterminism: 3,409/3,470/3,422 steps, val at 2 loops 0.0824/0.0894/0.0912 (seed 2's pretrained model is the worst of the six and finished lowest). No forgetting: held-out greedy 0.984/0.986/0.985. RL charged 1,678/1,710/1,731 s with 122/90/69 s left; no crash. Caveat on the keep: like 509, one seed carries the mean. Next: the entropy reading says the fine-tune's epochs over the found proofs set the policy's peakedness and pass@64 pays for less of it; test it directly by holding rounds fixed and varying epochs (FT_RECORDS at one epoch of the mix, or RL_WEIGHT 4 -> 1), or raise sampling temperature in RL, and watch new-proofs-per-pass against per-sample accuracy. Depth did not get more valuable here and the gap in theorems got smaller. |

Seeds 0 and 2 moved +3 and -9; the mean loss is seed 1 (-49 against the loop's high outlier 815). The pre-registered 'parameters are the bottleneck' reading is falsified: the mean is below 764 and per-sample dev accuracy at 8 loops is within 0.01 of 510's on two seeds (0.467/0.442/0.444 against 0.461/0.481/0.443; seed 1 -0.039), so matching the untied control's parameter count (9,580,544 against 590's 9,558,528) with a wider tied trunk does not close the gap to 792. With 506 (untied first pass, 9.56M, -25) this is the second way of spending the spare 3.2M that bought nothing, and this one changed neither the architecture nor the loop schedule nor the RL. Pretraining went the capacity way, RL did not. Val loss at 2 loops 0.0791/0.0872/0.0887 (mean 0.0850) against 0.0824/0.0894/0.0912 (0.0877), lower on every seed by 0.002-0.003 with 21% fewer steps (2,687/2,688/2,697 against 3,409/3,470/3,422; the bench said 0.79x), depth-flat within 0.0004 from 2 to 8 loops as always; held-out greedy after pretraining 0.947/0.954/0.948 (510: 0.943/0.960/0.965). The pretrained model also started RL stronger on two seeds: round-1 one-loop acceptance 0.161/0.199/0.039 (510: 0.048/0.111/0.061) and 700/731/257 targets solved after round 1 (510: 261/723/343). From round 5 on the advantage was gone: one-loop acceptance at matched rounds 5-10 was 0.569-0.647 on seed 0 against 510's 0.587-0.653 (equal or 0.01-0.02 lower), 0.575-0.646 on seed 1 against 0.579-0.664 (0.00-0.04 lower), 0.553-0.666 on seed 2 against 0.569-0.651 (mixed); last round 0.649/0.646/0.666 (510: 0.671/0.667/0.634; predicted 0.66-0.76, two seeds under). RL discovery at matched round 10 (call 40) was 1,243/1,254/1,247 against 510's 1,239/1,294/1,230 and 590's 1,264: equal within seed noise. So 1.5x the parameters in every block fit the found proofs no better per round and generalize no better per sample; the extra capacity shows only in the pretraining loss and in round 1, which (507, 509) predict nothing. Compare the control: 590's untied model reaches one-loop acceptance 0.769 at round 5 and 0.835 at round 13 under 507's recipe, where 509 (the looped trunk under the closest recipe) had 0.638 at round 5 and 0.734 at its last round, 11: the untied blocks fit their own proofs far better per round than any tied core so far, wide or narrow. That points the 792 gap at tying (the shared core's converged iteration, 505) or at RL budget (590 ran 20 rounds because its retries cost 6 blocks per token at every level), not at parameter count or pretraining fit (505 and 508 already showed lower val loss reaching nothing). Costs as predicted or milder: rounds 11/10/10 (predicted 9-11; 510: 13/14/12); rounds 3+ took 134-158/137-174/129-177 s (predicted 140-175; 510: 102-142); fine-tune 35-52 s per round at 0.128 s/step (510: 27-42 s, 0.103 s/step; predicted 55-75, too high), ft_steps 293-393 as 510; sampling slowed less than the 0.75x assumed: 1-loop 173-223 samples/s (510: 201-249), 8-loop retries 68-96 (510: 70-117), 8-loop eval 68/74/81 (510: 83/87/90); eval sampling 1,041/953/877 s at 8 loops and 541/424/406 s at 2 (510: 850/816/789 and 379/381/371); totals 4,286/4,021/3,982 s (predicted 4,300-4,700), 1,100 s inside TOTAL_SECS; no OOM at the 8-loop eval. Cumulative RL solved 1,253/1,254/1,247 (510: 1,264/1,314/1,243). Loops unchanged, as pre-registered: metric minus diag +19 (14/21/21; 510: +12 = 12/20/5), per-sample 8-vs-2 gap 0.039/0.041/0.036 (510: 0.039/0.037/0.026), retry crack rates pooled 16.3/22.0/21.2, 15.4/19.9/21.5, 16.5/16.8/18.6% at 2/4/8 loops (510: 15.1/18.1/19.0, 20.0/23.8/24.9, 15.3/17.0/17.1), rounds 3+ 14.7/19.2/18.2, 14.3/19.1/20.2, 19.5/19.3/20.6. Held-out greedy after RL 0.986/0.977/0.985 (510: 0.984/0.986/0.985). pass@64 at 8 loops by length, seed 0: 108/129/380/99/23/6/1 at lengths 7-13 (510 seed 0: 104/114/389/106/24/5/1). 7 patch lines, one of them code; pods 74-80 min, about $1.90 plus a $0.08 bench. Next: separate the two remaining readings at equal RL rounds. Either cap the untied control at 10-11 rounds, or give the looped trunk 590's round count by retrying at 2 loops only (cheap rounds; 502 says 2 loops cracks 11% of resistant targets against 16% at 8, at 2.5x less cost per sample): if the looped model then approaches 792 the deficit is RL budget; if it stays near 760 it is tying, and the next architecture question is a core with more distinct functions per loop at the same compute (two alternating shared cores, 9.5M), not a wider one. |
